terms.ascender: The part of a lowercase letter that rises above the x-height, as in b, d and h.
terms.baseline: The line that most letters sit on.
terms.descender: The part of a letter that falls below the baseline, as in g, p and y.
terms.em: A unit of space equal to the current type size.
terms.glyph: A single drawn shape in a font, such as a letter, figure or ligature.
terms.kerning: Adjusting the space between two particular letters.
terms.leading: The vertical distance from one baseline to the next.
terms.ligature: Two or more letters joined into one glyph, such as fi or fl.
terms.serif: A small stroke at the end of a letter's main strokes.
terms.tracking: Adjusting the space evenly across a run of letters.
terms.typeface: A family of related fonts that share one design.
terms.x-height: The height of lowercase letters without ascenders, such as x.
